findings.reason: The protected solution is a concise, conventional sliding window over a fixed 26-letter table. Its left, right, character, frequencies, and best names expose the algorithm directly, and recomputing the fixed-size maximum keeps the invariant especially clear; no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 424 and its Python characterReplacement surface. The Reference preserves the replacement operation, at-most-k budget, longest contiguous repeated-letter result, both source examples with complete explanations, and all three constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064773604. Apart from the required Solution method wrapper, it is structurally identical to the app-local source: both update the same 26 counters, shrink on window length minus maximum frequency, remove the same left character, and record the same maximum window length.

The legal 64-, 192-, and 512-character full-budget tiers span 8x and force exhaustive work from substring enumeration while the window remains feasible. The current source passes all 12 executions at 0.97x the protected reference runtime; a correct quadratic control passes every output but fails only the runtime verdict at 222.82x.

The Approach derives the window deficit as length minus maximum frequency, explains why an infeasible left boundary can be discarded, matches the implementation's exact-frequency shrink loop, and accurately states O(n) time with O(1) fixed-alphabet space.
The hash-bound public Reference preserves the complete replacement model, both source examples and every explanatory step, all three constraints, and the absence of source visuals or tables.
